request: User asks for attractive parallax and scroll design that does not feel like a generic AI template
title: Add editorial parallax and scroll-led portfolio
purpose: Replace repetitive cards with distinctive typography, layered art and native scroll choreography

files.purpose: Build an editorial visual system with responsive native-scroll transformations.
files.previous_behavior: Uniform white and blue card grids with a static process diagram.
files.new_behavior: Warm paper palette, large typography, metal P artwork, asymmetric project grid, sticky desktop hero and service heading, and desktop scroll-driven decorative layers.
files.data_impact: None: static presentation and ephemeral DOM styles only; no operational data reads, writes or schemas.
files.access_control_impact: None: public content with no authentication or permission changes.
risks: Fixed-height project artwork can crop decorative content; essential project text is outside artwork.
Korean typography uses installed system fonts.
files.rollback: Revert this commit including all three source files to restore the prior static redesign. No data migration or operational rollback.

files.purpose: Implement event-driven parallax without React rerenders or intercepting native scrolling.
files.previous_behavior: No client-side scroll choreography on the redesigned homepage.
files.new_behavior: Passive listener batches geometry reads and CSS variable writes in requestAnimationFrame. Desktop media queries and live reduced-motion changes enable/disable motion; SVG sculpture stays visible without JavaScript.
files.data_impact: None: static presentation and ephemeral DOM styles only; no operational data reads, writes or schemas.
files.access_control_impact: None: public content with no authentication or permission changes.
risks: Scroll geometry queries add work per active scroll frame; runtime testing was in Chromium only.
Mobile and short-height viewports intentionally render static artwork rather than pinned motion.
files.rollback: Revert this commit including all three source files to restore the prior static redesign. No data migration or operational rollback.

production_safety.operational_data: No production operational data read, created, updated or deleted.
external_side_effects: Local build and browser tests only; no production deployment, Git push, messages or form submission. Existing project and email destinations preserved.

verification.evidence: No errors or warnings in changed TSX files.
Next.js compilation, TypeScript validation and static route generation passed after final edits.
Hero transform matrix changed after scrolling 450px. No missing anchor targets. FAQ opens. No page errors. Screenshots inspected on desktop and mobile.

verification.command: Playwright viewport and accessibility preference checks
verification.evidence: No horizontal overflow at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440px. Mobile data-motion=false; reduced motion data-motion=false and hero position=relative. Heading visible with JavaScript disabled.
Recorded approximately 15 seconds of native scrolling through hero and portfolio into pluck-scroll-preview.webm.
Known unmodified legacy smooth-scroll.tsx hook error and line-reveal.tsx unused variable from prior turn. Changed-file lint and full build passed.

residual_risks: Not deployed; external project destinations and email delivery not retested.
Cross-browser Safari/Firefox and low-powered device frame rate not measured.
Existing unused motion files retain their previously documented full-repository lint issues.
